meta.source: Coded from the published QP and mark scheme (4MA1_1F_2311). Derived metadata only. No exam question text transcribed.

coding_notes: q15 tagged set_notation — the skill added 2026-10-07 once the candidate cleared the four-part bar. Listing the members of a complement, an intersection and a union-with-complement. No n(), consistent with every other coded Foundation paper.

q24 FIRST SIGHTING of trigonometry_missing_angles in the corpus — it had zero parts across the first twelve papers. The question looks like a sine-rule problem and is on a FOUNDATION paper, which would have been a tier finding; it is not. The mark scheme's primary route drops a perpendicular and uses right-angled trigonometry (tan 40 = 8/AD, then tan x = 8/DB). Sine and cosine rule appear only as 'oe' alternatives a Higher student might reach for. Tagged missing_angles first because an angle is what is asked for.

q3(a) tagged angles_on_lines_and_circles for naming an angle by type, following the house precedent in docs/coding-a-paper.md (there is no 'classify an angle' node, and measuring_lines_and_angles costs more while claiming protractor use).
q1(a)(ii) and q1(c) tagged indices for a cube number and a square root — the house rule puts roots on indices.

q4(d) tagged properties_of_2d_shapes: completing a kite is about knowing what a kite is. reflections would be the geometric description but costs 7, including Understanding Straight Line Graphs and Function Machines, for one mark of a Foundation question.
mark_split follows the mark scheme's codes where extraction is unambiguous and the standard Edexcel shape for the mark count otherwise.
